content:
# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 6

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 22

---

## Disagreement 001 — v. 1: "old Athenian"

- **EMET:** "an old Athenian"
- **LOGOS:** "an Athenian elder"
- **PNEUMA:** "an elderly Athenian official"
- **Note:** Greek *presbuteron Athēnaion* — an elder/old man from Athens. LOGOS's "elder" is slightly formal. PNEUMA adds "official" not in the Greek. SOPHIA uses "elderly Athenian."

## Disagreement 002 — v. 2: Zeus-Hospitius / Zeus-the-Friend-of-Strangers

- **EMET:** "Zeus-the-Friend-of-Strangers"
- **LOGOS:** "Zeus-Hospitius"
- **PNEUMA:** "Zeus-the-Friend-of-Strangers"
- **Note:** Greek *Zeus Xenios*. LOGOS uses the Latin epithet "Hospitius" as a conventional translation. EMET/PNEUMA translate. SOPHIA uses "Zeus-Hospitius" as the more standard scholarly rendering.

## Disagreement 003 — v. 2: "as the inhabitants of that place indeed were"

- **EMET:** "as the inhabitants of that place indeed were"
- **LOGOS:** "as the inhabitants of that place had requested"
- **PNEUMA:** "a title that apparently suited its worshipers just fine"
- **Note:** Greek *kathōs etychon oi ten topon oikountes* — as happened to be the case for the inhabitants. EMET's "indeed were" and LOGOS's "had requested" give different readings. PNEUMA's rendering is interpretive and snide. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 004 — v. 3: Summary statement

- **EMET:** "Harsh and utterly grievous was the onset of evil"
- **LOGOS:** "Harsh and utterly grievous was the oppression that came"
- **PNEUMA:** "What followed was a brutal and overwhelming catastrophe"
- **Note:** Greek *chalepē de kai tois pollois bareia katantēsis kakōn* — a hard and heavy onset of evils. PNEUMA paraphrases. EMET and LOGOS are closer. SOPHIA uses "oppression that befell them."

## Disagreement 005 — v. 4: Temple defilement

- **EMET:** "dallied with prostitutes and had intercourse with women"
- **LOGOS:** "consorted with prostitutes and had intercourse with women"
- **PNEUMA:** "Gentiles slept with prostitutes in the sacred precincts"
- **Note:** PNEUMA omits the specific mention of "women" as distinct from prostitutes in the inner precincts. EMET "dallied" is too mild for the Greek *synousiazontes*. SOPHIA uses "consorted."

## Disagreement 006 — v. 5: Altar's defilement

- **EMET:** "covered with abominable offerings that were forbidden by the laws"
- **LOGOS:** "piled with unlawful offerings that the law forbade"
- **PNEUMA:** "heaped with prohibited offerings — everything the law condemned"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "everything the law condemned" as an expansion. All three are accurate. SOPHIA uses LOGOS's phrasing.

## Disagreement 007 — v. 6: "confess to being a Jew"

- **EMET:** "simply acknowledge oneself to be a Jew"
- **LOGOS:** "confess to being a Jew"
- **PNEUMA:** "admit out loud that you were a Jew"
- **Note:** Greek *homologein Ioudaion einai*. "Acknowledge" (EMET) vs. "confess" (LOGOS) vs. "admit" (PNEUMA). "Confess" has the double meaning of religious confession. SOPHIA uses "confess to being a Jew."

## Disagreement 008 — v. 7: Dionysiac procession

- **EMET:** "wearing wreaths of ivy"
- **LOGOS:** "wearing garlands of ivy"
- **PNEUMA:** "crowned with ivy wreaths"
- **Note:** "Wreaths" vs. "garlands" for Greek *kissou stephanous*. "Garlands" (LOGOS) is standard. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 009 — v. 11: Death by burning

- **EMET:** "were informed upon and burned together"
- **LOGOS:** "were denounced to Philip, and were all burned together"
- **PNEUMA:** "They were betrayed. Philip came and burned them alive inside the caves"
- **Note:** LOGOS names Philip (the governor of Jerusalem from ch. 5); EMET and PNEUMA omit or embed the name. PNEUMA adds "inside the caves" for clarity. SOPHIA includes Philip's name per LOGOS.

## Disagreement 010 — v. 12: Authorial address

- **EMET:** "not to be depressed by such calamities"
- **LOGOS:** "not to be dismayed by these calamities"
- **PNEUMA:** "do not let these horrors drive you to despair"
- **Note:** "Depressed" (EMET) is too mild. "Dismayed" (LOGOS) is accurate. "Despair" (PNEUMA) is stronger than the Greek *ekkakein* — to grow faint/discouraged. SOPHIA uses "dismayed."

## Disagreement 011 — v. 13: God's swift punishment as kindness

- **EMET:** "it is a sign of great kindness not to let the impious alone for long"
- **LOGOS:** "it is a mark of great favor that the impious are not left long undisturbed"
- **PNEUMA:** "It is actually a sign of God's goodness that the wicked are punished quickly"
- **Note:** Greek *euergesias sēmeion* — sign of beneficence/favor. PNEUMA adds "God's" and substitutes "quickly" for the temporal construction. SOPHIA uses "mark of great kindness."

## Disagreement 012 — v. 14: The nations vs. Israel

- **EMET:** "the Sovereign Lord waits patiently until they have reached the full measure of their sins before punishing them"
- **LOGOS:** "the Sovereign Lord waits patiently until they have reached the full measure of their sins before he punishes them"
- **PNEUMA:** "he lets their sins accumulate to their full measure before he acts"
- **Note:** All three agree. PNEUMA slightly paraphrases. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 013 — v. 18: Eleazar's description

- **EMET:** "one of the leading scribes, a man already advanced in years and of noble presence"
- **LOGOS:** "one of the chief scribes, a man of advanced years and distinguished bearing"
- **PNEUMA:** "one of the most distinguished scholars of the law — an old man of noble bearing and great reputation"
- **Note:** PNEUMA expands "scribes" to "scholars of the law" and adds "great reputation." Greek *grammateis* — scribes/scholars. SOPHIA uses "leading scribes" for precision.

## Disagreement 014 — v. 19: Eleazar's choice

- **EMET:** "welcoming death with honor rather than life with pollution"
- **LOGOS:** "preferring an honorable death to a life of defilement"
- **PNEUMA:** "He chose an honorable death over a defiled life"
- **Note:** "Welcoming" vs. "preferring" vs. "chose." LOGOS is most felicitous. Greek *hairetisas* — choosing/preferring. SOPHIA uses "welcoming" to preserve the active, voluntary quality.

## Disagreement 015 — v. 19: "rack" vs. "instrument of torture"

- **EMET:** "went up to the rack of his own accord"
- **LOGOS:** "went forward to the instrument of torture of his own accord"
- **PNEUMA:** "He walked up to the instrument of torture himself"
- **Note:** Greek *to tympanon* — the tympanum/rack (a drum-shaped instrument for stretching/beating). "Rack" (EMET) is specific but may evoke a different torture device. SOPHIA uses "instrument of torture" per LOGOS.

## Disagreement 016 — v. 23: The resolve described

- **EMET:** "making a high resolve, worthy of his years and the dignity of his old age and the gray hairs which he had reached with such distinction"
- **LOGOS:** "making a decision worthy of his years and the dignity of old age and the distinguished gray hairs he had attained"
- **PNEUMA:** "It was a choice worthy of everything he was: his years, his dignity, his magnificent white hair earned through a life well lived"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "magnificent white hair earned through a life well lived" is an interpretive expansion. EMET's "high resolve" is slightly archaic. SOPHIA uses "a resolve worthy of his years and the dignity of his old age and the distinguished gray hairs he had attained."

## Disagreement 017 — v. 23: "send him to Hades"

- **EMET:** "telling them to send him to Hades"
- **LOGOS:** "telling them to send him to Hades at once"
- **PNEUMA:** "He answered them immediately: send me to Hades"
- **Note:** All three preserve this crucial line. LOGOS adds "at once" for emphasis. PNEUMA converts to first-person speech. SOPHIA follows EMET for brevity and impact.

## Disagreement 018 — v. 24: The deceptive appearance to the young

- **EMET:** "many of the young should suppose that Eleazar in his ninetieth year has gone over to an alien religion"
- **LOGOS:** "many of the young might suppose that Eleazar in his ninetieth year has gone over to an alien religion"
- **PNEUMA:** "the young men thought that Eleazar — at ninety years old — had converted to a foreign religion"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "converted" is interpretively accurate. "Gone over to an alien religion" (EMET/LOGOS) is more literal. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 019 — v. 27: "worthy of my old age"

- **EMET:** "I will show myself worthy of my old age"
- **LOGOS:** "I shall show myself worthy of my old age"
- **PNEUMA:** "I will prove I am worthy of the age I have reached"
- **Note:** All convey the same. PNEUMA slightly expands. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 020 — v. 28: Legacy to the young

- **EMET:** "a noble example of how to die a good death willingly and nobly"
- **LOGOS:** "a noble example of how to die willingly and courageously"
- **PNEUMA:** "a clear example of how to choose death over compromise, and how to die well"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "choose death over compromise" not in the Greek. LOGOS uses "courageously" for Greek *gennaios*. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 021 — v. 30: Bystanders' change

- **EMET:** "those who a little before had been acting with goodwill now changed to ill will"
- **LOGOS:** "those who just before had been treating him with goodwill turned to hostility"
- **PNEUMA:** "The men who had tried to help him now turned against him"
- **Note:** "Ill will" (EMET) vs. "hostility" (LOGOS) for Greek *dysmeneia*. SOPHIA uses "hostility."

## Disagreement 022 — v. 31: "I fear him"

- **EMET:** "I am glad to suffer these things because I fear him"
- **LOGOS:** "I am content to endure this because of my fear of him"
- **PNEUMA:** "my soul is at peace in this suffering, because I am in awe of him"
- **Note:** "Fear" vs. "awe" for Greek *diа ton autou phobon*. PNEUMA's "in awe" is softer; "fear" is more literal. SOPHIA uses "because of my fear of him."
